name: Desirability, Feasibility, and Viability (DFV) Mapping
phase: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that our cross-functional team holds strategic alignment on our core business vulnerabilities. We will verify this by mapping all operational assumptions across a 2 × 2 matrix (Impact vs. Evidence), and consider it validated if participants achieve ≥ 90% consensus on the top 5 assumptions categorized in the High Impact / Low Evidence quadrant.

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Assemble product, engineering, design and commercial leads with desirability, feasibility, viability cards.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Have each write their explicit premises, then place every assumption on a shared impact-by-evidence grid.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Cluster overlapping cards into themes and isolate high-impact, low-evidence as the experiment backlog.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Assemble product, engineering, design, and commercial leaders. Provide each member with assumption tracking cards categorized into Desirability, Feasibility, and Viability.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Instruct members to independently document explicit operational premises. Place every assumption onto a shared 2 × 2 grid: Vertical Axis = Impact (Low vs. High); Horizontal Axis = Current Evidence (Known vs. Unknown).

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Cluster overlapping cards into distinct operational themes. Isolate the High Impact / Low Evidence quadrant as the designated experiment backlog.

warning.label: HiPPO Distortion
warning.text: Senior executives drag risky assumptions into the known quadrant on personal conviction.

warningFull: Senior executives frequently drag high-risk assumptions into the "Known" quadrant based entirely on personal conviction, blinding the team to critical structural vulnerabilities.
